summary: Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and indology. He held positions at Visva-Bharati University (~1946–1949), Peking University (~1949–1952), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. Hou was a doctoral student at Ghent University and served there as a postdoctoral researcher (attested 2026).
Xiaoting Wei focuses on sinology and Buddhist studies. Wei earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng Mei Ku (attested 2004).

Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Peking University (~1954–1958). Huang later served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1979) and taught Jiang Yili.

Xinru Liu works in history, archaeology, indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing a PhD under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), Liu held posts at CASS (~1985–2002) and The College of New Jersey (~2002).
Xiuzhi Zeng specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zeng completed an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xue Yu works in Buddhist and religious studies. Yu held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Xuesong Zhang specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and became an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, tibetology, and indology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li held a fellowship at Ryukoku University (2011) and posts at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017, 2026).
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Yadi Qu works in computational fields, indology, and tibetology, and studied and held a position as a scientific project collaborator at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Yael Bentor specializes in tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington (PhD supervised by Gregory Schopen), Bentor taught Indian studies and became a professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Yakupitiyage Karunadasa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD under David Friedman at SOAS and the University of London. Karunadasa directed PGIPBS (~1991–2000) and held visiting professorships at SOAS, Calgary, Toronto, and HKU.
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies and sinology, and completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An specializes in Buddhist studies and indology. An completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (attested 1998) and also studied under Hojin (attested 2003).
Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in tibetology who completed a PhD under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao at SOAS University of London (~1999–2004).
Yanling Chen focuses on Buddhist studies. Chen earned an MA at Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2012).
Yannick Laurent works in tibetology, history, and archaeology. Laurent held posts at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (both attested 2026).
Yanpei was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Taixu (~1934–1939) and Yinshun (~1941–1947).

Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (1997), Tsai became a Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
